'''''Aira praecox''''' is a species of [[Poaceae|grass]] known by several common names, including '''early hair-grass''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17}}</ref> '''yellow hairgrass''' and '''spike hairgrass'''. It is native to [[Europe]], where it is found in dry, sandy places, on rocky outcrops, and in heath [[grassland]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Early Hair-grass {{!}} NatureSpot|url=https://www.naturespot.org.uk/species/early-hair-grass|access-date=2021-04-23|website=www.naturespot.org.uk}}</ref> It also grows in North America as an [[introduced species]], where it can be found on the east and west coasts in sandy or rocky areas, such as beaches and roadsides. This is a tuft-forming annual grass growing up to about 10 to 15 centimeters in maximum height.<ref name=Stace>{{cite book|last=Stace|first=C. A.|author-link = Stace, C. A.|year=2019|title=New Flora of the British Isles|edition=Fourth|publisher=C & M Floristics|location = Middlewood Green, Suffolk, U.K.| isbn=978-1-5272-2630-2}}</ref>{{rp|1073}} The thin, narrow leaves are located at the base of the stem, and are typically 0.3–2 millimeters wide.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Aira praecox (early silver-hairgrass): Go Botany|url=https://gobotany.nativeplanttrust.org/species/aira/praecox/|access-date=2021-04-23|website=gobotany.nativeplanttrust.org}}</ref> It bears small, tightly congested [[inflorescence]]s of purple-tinted green [[Plant sexuality|bisexual]] spikelets.

It is an annual, forming low and small but  numerous tufts.  It flowers from April to June.<ref name=":0" />

Certain moths and butterflies, including the [[Grayling (butterfly)|Grayling butterfly]] and the [[Euxoa cursoria|Coast Dart moth]], feed on it as [[larva]]e.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Moths larvae that feed on Early Hair-grass Aira praecox {{!}} Northumberland Moths|url=https://www.northumberlandmoths.org.uk/foodplants.php?foodplant=Aira%20praecox|access-date=2021-04-23|website=www.northumberlandmoths.org.uk}}</ref>
